paper.title: Gaussian Process Optimization with Adaptive Sketching: Scalable and No Regret

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian process optimization / kernelized bandit with finite arm set (frequentist, ||f||_H <= F)
unmapped: reward function in RKHS with ||f||_H <= F (F mapped to S)
noise N(0, xi^2); appendix notes extension to xi-sub-Gaussian noise
settings.definition_quote: we assume that $\armset \triangleq \{\bx_i\}_{i=1}^{\Narm}$ is a fixed finite set of $\Narm$ vectors in $\Real^d$. ... receives reward $y_t \triangleq f(\bx_t) + \eta_t$ ... The goal of the learner is to minimize its cumulative regret $R_T \triangleq \sum_{t=1}^T f(\bx_\star) - f(\bx_t)$

symbols.d_eff: effective dimension d_eff(lambda, X_T) = Tr(K_T (K_T + lambda I)^{-1}) of the arms selected by BKB

conditions: noise eta_t ~ N(0, xi^2) with xi denoted sigma
tuning: beta_t = 2 xi sqrt(alpha log(kappa^2 t) sum_s sigma_tilde_t^2(x_s) + log(1/delta)) + (1 + 1/sqrt(1-epsilon)) sqrt(lambda) F

source.label: thm:main-regret
source.quote: Assume $\normsmall{f}_{\rkhs} \leq F < \infty$. For any desired $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, $0 < \delta < 1$, $0 < \lambda$, let $\alpha \triangleq (1 + \varepsilon)/(1 - \varepsilon)$ and $\qbar \geq 6\alpha\log(4T/\delta)/\varepsilon^2$. If we run \bkb with $\wt{\beta}_t \triangleq ...$ then, with probability of at least $1-\delta$, the regret $R_T$ of \bkb is bounded as $R_T \leq 2(2\alpha)^{3/2}\sqrt{T}(\xi\deff(\lambda,\wt{\bX}_T)\log(\kappa^2T) +\sqrt{\lambda \fnorm^2 \deff(\lambda,\wt{\bX}_T)\log(\kappa^2T)}+ \xi\log(1/\delta) )$.

results.notes: Regret is realized sum f(x*)-f(x_t) bounded w.p. 1-delta. d_eff is data-dependent (depends on arms selected). Per-step time O(A d_eff^2) up to logs (Theorem 1, a dictionary-size/accuracy guarantee, not recorded as a regret result). Paper's lambda=xi^2 in GP view but theorem allows any lambda>0.
